name: Nuestra Señora de Atocha
value: ~$400M recovered: 40 t silver & gold, emeralds, 100,000 silver coins
summary: Flagship-escort of the 1622 Tierra Firme fleet, sunk by a hurricane off the Florida Keys. Found by Mel Fisher in 1985 after a 16-year search ("Today's the day!"). The sterncastle — with much of the registered treasure — has never been found.

name: Atocha sterncastle (missing section)
value: Est. $200M+ of unrecovered silver, gold and emeralds
summary: The stern of the Atocha broke away and drifted in a second hurricane. Historians believe a large share of the manifested gold and contraband emeralds was carried there. Still being searched by the Fisher company.

name: Santa Margarita
value: Gold bars, silver, a 1.8 kg gold chain; more still missing
summary: Sister ship of the Atocha in the 1622 fleet. Partly salvaged by the Spanish in the 1620s, rediscovered in 1980. Finds continue — gold and silver were still being recovered in the 2000s.

name: San José (1708)
value: Est. $4–20 billion in gold, silver and emeralds — the "holy grail of shipwrecks"
summary: Blown up by a British squadron in Wager's Action near Cartagena while carrying Peruvian silver and gold. Located in 2015; the exact position is a Colombian state secret and ownership is disputed between Colombia, Spain, Bolivian Qhara Qhara people and Sea Search Armada.

name: Flor de la Mar
value: Plunder of Malacca — 60 t gold, jewels; est. $2.6 billion
summary: Afonso de Albuquerque's flagship sank in a storm in the Strait of Malacca carrying the loot of the conquest of Malacca. Often called the richest ship ever lost. Never conclusively found; the area lies between Indonesia and Malaysia.

name: Nuestra Señora de las Mercedes
value: 594,000 silver & gold coins (17 t), ~$500M
summary: Blown up by the Royal Navy off Cape Santa Maria, Portugal. Odyssey Marine salvaged the coins in 2007; a US court awarded the entire hoard to Spain in 2012.

name: SS Central America
value: ~30,000 lb (13.6 t) of California Gold Rush gold; contributed to the Panic of 1857
summary: The "Ship of Gold" sank in a hurricane off the Carolinas. Thompson's team recovered gold bars and coins worth ~$100–150M; Thompson later fled and was jailed for contempt over missing coins.

name: SS Republic (1853)
value: 51,000+ gold and silver coins, ~$75M
summary: Sank in a hurricane off Georgia en route to New Orleans carrying $400,000 in coins (1865 value) for post-Civil War reconstruction.

name: SS Gairsoppa
value: 110 t of silver (≈$210M) — deepest, largest precious-metal recovery
summary: British India Steam Navigation ship torpedoed by U-101 southwest of Ireland. Silver recovered from 4,700 m in 2012–2013.

name: Whydah Gally
value: Gold, silver, jewellery of 50+ plundered ships; only part recovered
summary: Flagship of "Black Sam" Bellamy, the richest pirate in history, wrecked in a nor'easter off Cape Cod. The only fully authenticated Golden Age pirate shipwreck. Excavation still ongoing.

name: Queen Anne's Revenge
value: Cannons, gold dust traces; no major treasure
summary: Blackbeard's flagship ran aground at Beaufort Inlet, North Carolina. Blackbeard's rumoured treasure has never been found.

name: 1715 Treasure Fleet
value: 14 million pesos registered; finds still wash up on the "Treasure Coast"
summary: Eleven of twelve ships were wrecked by a hurricane along Florida's east coast. Several wrecks are still unlocated, and gold coins are still found on the beaches after storms (e.g. 2015: $4.5M).

name: 1715 Fleet — unlocated wrecks
value: Several galleons including the Capitana of Ubilla's fleet partly missing
summary: Of the 11 wrecks, several have never been positively identified — including the Nuestra Señora de la Regla and the El Señor San Miguel, rumoured to have survived and vanished.

name: 1733 Spanish Treasure Fleet
value: Silver coins, porcelain; much salvaged by Spain in 1733
summary: Wrecked by a hurricane along the Florida Keys. The San Pedro is now an underwater archaeological preserve.

name: Nuestra Señora de la Pura y Limpia Concepción
value: Silver, gold, Ming porcelain; William Phips recovered 34 t in 1687
summary: Wrecked on the Silver Bank north of Hispaniola. Phips's recovery made him rich and governor of Massachusetts; Burt Webber re-located it in 1978. Large quantities are still believed to be in the coral.

name: Las Cinco Chagas
value: Gold, diamonds, rubies — est. $1 billion
summary: Blown up after a fight with English privateers off the Azores while returning from India. Believed to rival the Flor de la Mar as the richest ship ever lost.

name: Merchant Royal
value: 100,000 lb gold, 400 bars Mexican silver, 500,000 pieces of eight — "El Dorado of the Seas" (~$1.5B)
summary: Sank in bad weather off Land's End, Cornwall. An anchor thought to be hers was dragged up by a trawler in 2019, but the wreck remains unfound.

name: San Diego (1600)
value: Ming porcelain, gold jewellery, astrolabes
summary: Converted merchant galleon sunk fighting the Dutch near Fortune Island, Philippines. 34,000 artefacts recovered.

name: Nuestra Señora del Pilar de Zaragoza
value: Silver from Acapulco bound for Manila
summary: Manila galleon wrecked at Cocos Island, Guam. Some silver coins have been recovered; the main wreck has never been located.

name: Nuestra Señora de la Concepción (1638)
value: Gold jewellery, jade, Ming porcelain
summary: One of the largest Manila galleons, wrecked on the reefs of Saipan. 1,300 pieces of gold jewellery were recovered in 1987–1990.

name: San Agustín (1595)
value: Chinese silk, porcelain, beeswax
summary: Wrecked in Drakes Bay, California — the first known shipwreck on the US west coast. Porcelain fragments wash up, but the hull has never been found.

name: Santo Cristo de Burgos ("Beeswax wreck")
value: Beeswax, porcelain; rumoured silver
summary: Manila galleon wrecked near Nehalem, Oregon. Beeswax blocks inscribed in Spanish washed ashore for centuries, inspiring local treasure legends at Neahkahnie Mountain.

name: El Cazador
value: 450,000 silver reales minted in Mexico
summary: Carried silver to shore up Spanish Louisiana's currency; its loss helped push Spain to sell Louisiana. Found by a fishing trawler whose net snagged coins.

name: Le Chameau
value: 289,000 livres in gold, silver coins for Louisbourg
summary: Wrecked near Louisbourg, Nova Scotia, carrying pay for the garrison. One of Canada's richest wrecks.

name: Royal Charter
value: £322,000 of Australian gold (1859); some still in the sand
summary: Returning from Melbourne's goldfields, wrecked on Anglesey in the "Royal Charter Storm". Passengers drowned weighed down by gold sewn into belts. Gold nuggets still occasionally found.

name: HMS Lutine
value: £1.2M in gold and silver (1799) — most never recovered
summary: Wrecked on the Vlieland sandbanks, Netherlands. Her bell hangs at Lloyd's of London. Shifting sands have defeated two centuries of salvage attempts.

name: HMS Sussex (1693)
value: Rumoured 9 t of gold coins to bribe the Duke of Savoy (~$4B); disputed
summary: Sank in a storm off Gibraltar. Odyssey Marine claimed to have found her in 2001 but work was halted by Spain. Whether she carried the gold is debated.

name: HMS Victory (1737)
value: Rumoured 4 t of Portuguese gold coins (~$1B)
summary: Predecessor of Nelson's Victory, lost in a storm in the English Channel. Found 100 km from where she was thought to have sunk. Recovery is restricted under UK law.

name: Grosvenor
value: Rumoured gold, diamonds, the Peacock Throne (legend)
summary: Wrecked on the Pondoland coast of South Africa. Some coins recovered; legends that it carried the Peacock Throne of the Mughals are unfounded but persist.

name: Batavia
value: 12 chests of silver coins, jewels
summary: Wrecked on the Houtman Abrolhos, Western Australia, on her maiden voyage — followed by a horrific mutiny and massacre among survivors.

name: Zuytdorp
value: 250,000 guilders in newly minted silver coins
summary: Wrecked on the cliffs of Western Australia. The site is in violent surf; a "carpet of silver" was reported in 1964.

name: Vergulde Draeck (Gilt Dragon)
value: 8 chests of silver, 78,600 guilders
summary: Wrecked off Western Australia. Survivors set off inland and vanished; legends say they buried the missing silver.

name: Geldermalsen ("Nanking Cargo")
value: 125 gold ingots, 160,000 pieces of Qing porcelain
summary: Sank after hitting a reef south of Singapore. Hatcher's 1986 auction of the "Nanking Cargo" at Christie's made $15M — and caused an archaeology scandal.

name: Tek Sing
value: 350,000 pieces of porcelain
summary: "The Titanic of the East" — a huge junk sunk in the Gaspar Strait with ~1,600 people. One of the largest porcelain cargoes ever found.

name: Belitung shipwreck
value: 60,000 Tang dynasty ceramics, gold and silver cups
summary: A 9th-century Arab dhow wrecked off Belitung Island, Indonesia — proof of the Maritime Silk Road. Its "Tang Treasure" is in Singapore.

name: Nanhai One
value: 180,000 artefacts: gold, silver, porcelain, coins
summary: A Southern Song merchant ship raised whole in a steel caisson in 2007 and excavated inside a museum in Yangjiang.

name: Antikythera wreck
value: Bronze statues, the Antikythera mechanism, coins, jewellery
summary: A 1st-century BC wreck that yielded the Antikythera mechanism — the world's oldest known analogue computer. Excavations still yield finds.

name: Uluburun shipwreck
value: 10 t of copper, tin, glass ingots, gold, ivory
summary: One of the oldest known shipwrecks (c. 1300 BC), off southern Turkey. Its cargo is a snapshot of the Late Bronze Age world economy.

name: Dmitrii Donskoi
value: Claimed 200 t gold (~$130B) — almost certainly a hoax
summary: Scuttled off Ulleungdo, Korea after the Battle of Tsushima. The 2018 "gold" announcement triggered a stock-fraud scandal.

name: Admiral Nakhimov (1885)
value: Rumoured gold and platinum; Japanese divers found nothing in 1980
summary: Sank after the Battle of Tsushima. Persistent legend of a gold cargo for paying the fleet.

name: Awa Maru
value: Rumoured 40 t gold, 12 t platinum, diamonds (~$5B)
summary: Sunk by USS Queenfish despite safe-conduct. China raised parts in 1977–80 and found tin and rubber, but not the rumoured gold.

name: I-52
value: 2 t of gold (146 bars) for German technology
summary: Sunk by aircraft from USS Bogue in the mid-Atlantic while carrying gold to Nazi Germany. Found at 5,240 m; the gold has not been raised.

name: HMS Edinburgh (16)
value: 4.5 t of Soviet gold (465 bars) — 431 recovered in 1981
summary: Carrying Stalin's payment for Lend-Lease, torpedoed in the Barents Sea. One of the deepest gold salvages ever. 34 bars still missing.

name: SS Laurentic (1908)
value: 43 t of gold — 22 bars still missing
summary: Hit mines off Lough Swilly, Ireland carrying gold to pay for munitions. The Navy recovered 3,186 bars by 1924; 22 bars (~$20M) remain.

name: RMS Niagara
value: 8 t of gold; 5 bars still missing
summary: Mined off New Zealand while carrying gold to pay for American munitions. 555 of 590 bars recovered in 1941.

name: SS Egypt
value: £1M gold and silver, recovered by Italian divers 1932
summary: Sank after a collision in fog off Ushant. The salvage pioneered deep-diving armoured suits.

name: SS John Barry
value: 3 million silver riyals recovered; rumoured $26M more silver
summary: Torpedoed off Oman while carrying Saudi silver riyals. Part recovered in 1994; rumours persist of a much larger secret cargo.

name: SS Brother Jonathan
value: 1,200+ gold coins recovered
summary: Hit an uncharted rock off Crescent City, California. One of the deadliest shipwrecks on the US Pacific coast.

name: SS Golden Gate
value: $1.4M of gold (1862 value)
summary: Caught fire and beached near Manzanillo, Mexico. Gold coins still turn up on the beach.

name: SS Yankee Blade
value: $153,000 in gold specie (1854)
summary: Ran aground at Point Arguello, California, racing for a bet. Some gold coins recovered in 1948 and 1970s.

name: San Pedro de Alcántara
value: ~4 million pesos silver and gold, salvaged in 1786–87
summary: Wrecked at Peniche, Portugal carrying South American silver and Tupac Amaru rebels as prisoners.

name: Wreck of the São Bento
value: Pepper, Ming porcelain, jewels
summary: Portuguese Indiaman wrecked at the Msikaba river mouth, South Africa.

name: Santa María de la Consolación
value: Silver from Potosí
summary: Ran aground near Isla Santa Clara (Isla del Muerto), Ecuador, while fleeing pirates who reportedly massacred the crew. Silver coins found there in 1997.

name: Jesús María de la Limpia Concepción ("La Capitana")
value: 10 million pesos silver, including the Potosí mint fraud coins
summary: Flagship of the South Seas Armada wrecked on Chanduy reef, Ecuador. Her silver revealed the Potosí debasement scandal.

name: Our Lady of the Rosary (Quedagh Merchant)
value: Kidd's plunder: silks, gold, silver
summary: Captain Kidd's prize ship, abandoned and burned off Catalina Island, Dominican Republic. Its cargo was never accounted for, feeding the legend of Kidd's treasure.

name: Adventure Galley
value: A 50 kg silver bar recovered in 2015 — later identified as lead
summary: Kidd scuttled her at Île Sainte-Marie, Madagascar — the old pirate haven. Clifford's "silver bar" turned out to be 95% lead.

name: Fiery Dragon
value: Chinese porcelain
summary: Pirate Condent's ship, scuttled at Île Sainte-Marie, Madagascar.

name: Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe & Conde de Tolosa
value: Mercury, gold jewellery, diamonds
summary: Two mercury galleons wrecked in a hurricane in Samaná Bay, Dominican Republic.

name: Rooswijk
value: Silver ingots and Mexican coins (30 chests)
summary: Wrecked on the Goodwin Sands, Kent, on her way to the East Indies.

name: Hollandia (1742)
value: 129 chests of silver; ~35,000 coins recovered
summary: Struck Gunner Rock in the Isles of Scilly on her maiden voyage with no survivors.

name: Slot ter Hooge
value: 3 t of silver bars and coins
summary: Wrecked on Porto Santo, Madeira. John Lethbridge salvaged much of her in 1725 with a primitive diving barrel.

name: Witte Leeuw
value: Wanli porcelain, pepper, diamonds (rumoured)
summary: Blew up in a battle with Portuguese carracks at Jamestown Bay, St Helena.

name: Akerendam
value: 57,000 gold and silver coins
summary: Wrecked on her maiden voyage off Runde, Norway. Divers found 6,000 gold and 51,000 silver coins in 1972.

name: La Girona
value: Gold jewellery, the famous gold salamander pendant
summary: Spanish Armada galleass wrecked at Lacada Point near the Giant's Causeway, Northern Ireland, with ~1,300 drowned. Her gold is in the Ulster Museum.

name: Tobermory galleon (San Juan de Sicilia)
value: Legend says 30 million ducats of Armada pay
summary: Armada ship blown up in Tobermory Bay, Isle of Mull. Four centuries of salvage hunts for the pay chest have produced only a few coins.

name: Santa María (Columbus)
value: Historic value — no treasure
summary: Columbus's flagship ran aground off Haiti on Christmas Day 1492. A 2014 claim by Barry Clifford was rejected by UNESCO; the wreck is still unlocated.

name: Spanish Armada wrecks (Scotland & Ireland)
value: Pay chests, officers' gold and plate
summary: Around 24 Armada ships were wrecked around Scotland and Ireland. Many sites are unknown and rumoured to hold coins.

name: Santíssimo Sacramento
value: Bronze cannons
summary: Wrecked on the Santo Antônio bank off Salvador, Brazil.

name: SS Príncipe de Asturias
value: Rumoured undeclared gold and bronze statues
summary: "The Spanish Titanic" sank off Ilhabela, Brazil. Rumours of smuggled gold persist.

name: SS Tubantia
value: Rumoured £2M in German gold hidden in Edam cheeses
summary: Torpedoed in the North Sea. The rumour of gold coins in cheeses has driven salvage efforts for a century.

name: RMS Lusitania
value: Rumoured munitions and gold (unproven)
summary: Torpedoed by U-20 off the Old Head of Kinsale, helping bring the US into WWI.

name: Vigo Bay treasure fleet
value: Legend of vast silver; most was actually unloaded before the battle
summary: Anglo-Dutch attack burned the Spanish silver fleet in Rande Strait. Jules Verne had Captain Nemo fund the Nautilus from Vigo's treasure.

name: Nuestra Señora del Juncal
value: ~1 million pesos in silver and gold
summary: Almiranta of the 1631 New Spain fleet, lost in a storm in the Bay of Campeche. Mexico's INAH is actively searching for her.

name: Nuestra Señora de las Maravillas
value: 5 million pesos; emerald cross and gold recovered 2022
summary: Collided with her own flagship and sank on the Little Bahama Bank. Allen Exploration recovered spectacular jewels in 2020–22.

name: 1554 Padre Island fleet
type: Spanish naos (Santa María de Yciar, San Esteban, Espíritu Santo)
value: Silver coins, gold bars
summary: Three ships wrecked on Padre Island, Texas — the oldest known shipwrecks in the US.

name: Tristán de Luna fleet
value: Colonial supplies
summary: Hurricane destroyed the fleet of an attempted Spanish colony at Pensacola Bay.

name: Diana (1816)
value: 24,000 pieces of Chinese porcelain
summary: Sank in the Strait of Malacca. Her porcelain cargo sold at Christie's in 1995.

name: SS Atlantic (1849)
value: $36,000 in gold & coins of the American Express Co.
summary: Sank in Lake Erie after a collision. A legal battle over salvage rights lasted decades.

name: HMS Hussar (1763)
value: Rumoured British Army payroll in gold (~$500M)
summary: Sank in New York's Hell Gate. Landfill may now cover the wreck; the gold payroll was most likely already unloaded.

name: HMS DeBraak
value: Rumoured Spanish gold — only ~650 coins found
summary: Capsized off Cape Henlopen, Delaware. Her rumoured gold made her one of America's most hunted wrecks; the salvage was an archaeological disaster.

name: El Salvador (1750)
value: 240,000 pesos of silver and gold
summary: One of the 1750 fleet wrecked in a hurricane off North Carolina's Outer Banks. Never found.

name: 't Vliegent Hart
value: 3 chests of gold coins and silver
summary: Wrecked on the Rassen shoals in the Scheldt estuary on her way out to the East Indies.

name: Nuestra Señora del Rosario (1622)
value: Silver ingots and coins
summary: Part of the 1622 fleet, wrecked near the Dry Tortugas.

name: Tortugas shipwreck (Buen Jesús y Nuestra Señora del Rosario)
value: Gold and silver, 1,200 silver coins
summary: The first deep-water wreck excavated entirely by robot (1990).

name: RMS Titanic
value: Passengers' jewellery; no bullion
summary: Struck an iceberg on her maiden voyage and sank in 2 h 40 min. Found 1985; the hull is being consumed by iron-eating bacteria.

name: HMHS Britannic
summary: Titanic's sister, mined in the Kea Channel, Greece. The largest ship lost in WWI.

name: SS Andrea Doria
summary: Collided with MS Stockholm in fog off Nantucket. "The Mount Everest of diving" — many divers have died on her.

name: MV Wilhelm Gustloff
value: Rumoured Amber Room crates (unproven)
summary: Torpedoed by Soviet submarine S-13 in the Baltic while evacuating East Prussia — the deadliest single ship sinking in history.

name: MV Goya
summary: Sunk by Soviet submarine L-3 in the Baltic; ~7,000 people died in minutes.

name: SS Karlsruhe (1905)
value: Possibly crates from Königsberg — Amber Room hunters' favourite
summary: Last ship out of Königsberg in Operation Hannibal, sunk by Soviet aircraft. Found in 2020 with crates in the hold — speculation it carried the Amber Room.

name: Bismarck
summary: Sunk by the Royal Navy after sinking HMS Hood. Lies upright on an extinct volcano 4.8 km down.

name: HMS Hood
summary: Exploded within minutes in the Denmark Strait after a hit from Bismarck; only 3 survived.

name: Yamato
summary: The heaviest battleship ever built, sunk by US aircraft during Operation Ten-Go.

name: Musashi
summary: Yamato's sister, sunk in the Sibuyan Sea during the Battle of Leyte Gulf.

name: USS Indianapolis
summary: Torpedoed after delivering the Hiroshima bomb parts. Survivors drifted 4 days among sharks.

name: USS Arizona
summary: Destroyed in the attack on Pearl Harbor. Still leaks oil — "the tears of the Arizona".

name: Mary Rose
summary: Henry VIII's flagship sank in the Solent; raised in 1982 and now in Portsmouth.

name: Vasa
summary: Capsized 1,300 m into her maiden voyage in Stockholm. Raised in 1961, 98% intact.

name: Mars (1563)
value: Gold and silver coins seen on wreck
summary: Swedish flagship exploded fighting the Danes off Öland. One of the largest ships of its time.

name: Kronan (1672)
value: 255 gold coins found 1982
summary: Capsized and exploded at the Battle of Öland. Largest gold coin find in Sweden.

name: Endurance
summary: Shackleton's ship crushed by Weddell Sea ice. Found in 2022 in remarkable condition, name still legible.

name: Quest
summary: Shackleton died aboard her in 1922. Found off Labrador in 2024.

name: HMS Erebus
summary: Franklin's lost expedition searching for the Northwest Passage. Found 2014 where Inuit oral history said it was.

name: HMS Terror
summary: Found in Terror Bay in 2016 after a tip from Inuk Sammy Kogvik.

name: HMS Endeavour (Lord Sandwich)
summary: Captain Cook's ship, scuttled at Newport, Rhode Island. Australia announced identification in 2022; RIMAP disputes it.

name: Le Griffon
value: Furs
summary: La Salle's ship, the first full-sized sailing ship on the upper Great Lakes, vanished with her crew. The "holy grail" of Great Lakes wrecks.

name: SS Edmund Fitzgerald
summary: Sank in a storm on Lake Superior with all hands, immortalised by Gordon Lightfoot.

name: RMS Empress of Ireland
summary: Sank in 14 minutes in the St. Lawrence River after a collision.

name: MV Doña Paz
summary: Collided with an oil tanker in the Tablas Strait — the deadliest peacetime maritime disaster.

name: MS Estonia
summary: Sank in a storm in the Baltic after her bow visor failed. Conspiracy theories about military cargo persist.

name: Costa Concordia
summary: Capsized off Isola del Giglio. Raised and towed away in 2014 — the largest salvage ever.

name: MS Zenobia
summary: Capsized off Larnaca, Cyprus on her maiden voyage. One of the world's top 10 wreck dives — close to you in Cyprus.

name: Edro III
summary: Ran aground near Sea Caves, Peyia, Cyprus in a storm and still sits on the rocks. A landmark of the Paphos coast.

name: Demetrios II
summary: Ran aground in rough seas off Paphos, Cyprus (near Kouklia / Aphrodite's Rock). The rusting hull is visible from shore.

name: SS Sultana
summary: Boiler explosion on the Mississippi with Union POWs aboard — America's worst maritime disaster. Remains lie under an Arkansas soybean field.

name: SS Mont-Blanc
summary: The Halifax Explosion: largest man-made explosion before the atomic bomb.

name: Mary Celeste
summary: Found drifting and abandoned in 1872 with no crew — the most famous ghost ship. Later deliberately wrecked off Haiti for insurance; remains identified (tentatively) in 2001.

name: SS Baychimo
value: Furs worth ~$1M (1931)
summary: Abandoned in Arctic ice off Alaska, she was sighted drifting unmanned for 38 years — last seen 1969. Fate unknown.

name: USS Cyclops (AC-4)
value: Manganese ore
summary: Vanished without trace in the Bermuda Triangle — the largest non-combat loss of life in US Navy history.

name: Carroll A. Deering
summary: Found aground at Diamond Shoals with food cooking and the crew gone. Theories range from piracy to mutiny.

name: Octavius (legend)
summary: Legend of a ship found off Greenland with her crew frozen at their posts, the captain mid-log entry from 13 years earlier.

name: Jenny (legend)
summary: Legendary schooner said to have been found frozen in Antarctic ice in 1860 with her crew preserved aboard.

name: København
summary: The world's largest sailing ship vanished after leaving Buenos Aires — no wreckage was ever confirmed.

name: SS Waratah
summary: "Australia's Titanic" vanished off South Africa's Wild Coast. Emlyn Brown searched for 22 years without success.

name: MV Derbyshire
summary: The largest British ship ever lost at sea, sunk by Typhoon Orchid. Twice the size of Titanic.

name: SS El Faro
summary: Sailed into Hurricane Joaquin and sank near the Bahamas with all hands.

name: HMS Victoria (1887)
summary: Sank off Tripoli, Lebanon, after a collision ordered by her own admiral. Stands vertically, bow buried in the seabed.

name: SMS Scharnhorst
summary: Admiral von Spee's flagship, sunk at the Battle of the Falkland Islands.

name: Scapa Flow German fleet
value: "Low-background steel" prized for radiation sensors
summary: The interned German fleet scuttled itself in Orkney. Seven wrecks remain, a world-class dive site.

name: Truk Lagoon ghost fleet
summary: Operation Hailstone destroyed the Japanese base in Chuuk; the "Ghost Fleet" is the world's largest ship graveyard dive site.

name: Ironbottom Sound
summary: Named for the dozens of warships sunk off Guadalcanal in 1942–43.

name: HMS Gloucester (1654)
summary: Wrecked off Norfolk carrying the future King James II, who nearly drowned. Announced in 2022 — "the most significant find since the Mary Rose".

name: HMS Thetis (1817)
value: $810,000 silver; salvage pioneered diving bells in 1831
summary: Wrecked at Cabo Frio, Brazil, with silver bullion; most was recovered in a heroic salvage by her crew.

name: Thistlegorm
value: Motorbikes, trucks, locomotives
summary: Bombed in the Red Sea. Her cargo of WWII vehicles makes her one of the world's most famous wreck dives.

name: H. L. Hunley
value: Lt. Dixon's lucky gold coin (found)
summary: The first submarine to sink an enemy warship (USS Housatonic), then vanished. Raised in 2000.

name: USS Thresher (SSN-593)
summary: Lost during deep-diving tests east of Cape Cod. Ballard's Titanic search was cover for surveying Thresher and Scorpion.

name: USS Scorpion (SSN-589)
summary: Lost southwest of the Azores with two nuclear torpedoes aboard. The cause remains debated.

name: K-141 Kursk
summary: Torpedo explosion during exercises in the Barents Sea. Most of the hull was raised in 2001.

name: K-129 (Golf II)
value: Nuclear missiles & codebooks
summary: Sank northwest of Hawaii. The CIA's Project Azorian used Howard Hughes's Glomar Explorer to secretly raise part of it in 1974. Exact location still classified.

name: K-278 Komsomolets
summary: Fire and sinking in the Norwegian Sea. Still leaking radiation from her reactor.

name: K-8
summary: Sank in the Bay of Biscay with 4 nuclear torpedoes after a fire.

name: Minerve (S647)
summary: Vanished off Toulon. Found 51 years later in 2019 after a renewed search.

name: Surcouf
summary: The largest submarine of her time disappeared near the Panama Canal, probably rammed by a freighter. Never found.

name: ARA San Juan (S-42)
summary: Imploded in the South Atlantic; found a year later by Ocean Infinity.

name: KRI Nanggala (402)
summary: Sank during a torpedo drill north of Bali; found broken in three pieces.

name: Titan (OceanGate)
summary: Imploded on a dive to the Titanic. Debris found 500 m from Titanic's bow.

name: U-864
value: 67 t of mercury, jet engine parts for Japan
summary: The only submarine ever sunk by another submerged submarine. Her leaking mercury is an environmental hazard off Norway.

name: U-534
value: Rumoured Nazi gold — none found when raised
summary: Raised in 1993 by a Danish businessman hoping for Nazi gold — he found only wine and Enigma machines.

name: U-869
summary: The "Shadow Divers" mystery U-boat off New Jersey, identified after 6 years and 3 diver deaths.

name: U-47 (Prien)
summary: Günther Prien's U-boat, which sank HMS Royal Oak in Scapa Flow, vanished in the North Atlantic.

name: I-400
summary: The largest submarine of WWII, built to bomb the Panama Canal. Scuttled by the US off Oahu.

name: HMS Affray
summary: The last Royal Navy submarine lost at sea, in Hurd Deep in the Channel.

name: USS Grunion
summary: Lost off Kiska in the Aleutians; found by the sons of her captain 65 years later.

name: INS Dakar
summary: Vanished en route from Britain to Haifa; found between Crete and Cyprus in 1999.

name: Pearl Harbor midget submarine (sunk by USS Ward)
summary: Sunk by USS Ward an hour before the air attack — the first American shot of the Pacific War.

name: Malaysia Airlines Flight 370
locNote: Search area along the Inmarsat "7th arc" in the southern Indian Ocean. Debris (flaperon) washed up on Réunion.
summary: Vanished en route from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing. The largest search in aviation history found only washed-up debris. Ocean Infinity resumed searching in 2025.

name: Amelia Earhart — Lockheed Electra 10E
locNote: Leading theories: crashed and sank near Howland Island, or landed on Nikumaroro (Gardner Island) 640 km SE.
summary: Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan disappeared looking for Howland Island during her round-the-world flight. A 2024 sonar "plane shape" turned out to be a rock.

name: Earhart: Nikumaroro hypothesis
summary: TIGHAR's theory: Earhart landed on the reef at Nikumaroro and died as a castaway. Bones found in 1940 were lost; artefacts are suggestive but inconclusive.

name: Flight 19
summary: A training flight lost over the Bermuda Triangle; a PBM Mariner rescue plane also vanished (13 more dead). The legend that launched the Triangle myth.

name: Glenn Miller — UC-64 Norseman
summary: The bandleader vanished over the English Channel flying to Paris. One theory: hit by bombs jettisoned by returning RAF Lancasters.

name: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry — P-38 Lightning
value: His silver identity bracelet was found by a fisherman (1998)
summary: The author of The Little Prince disappeared on a reconnaissance flight. Wreckage found off Marseille; a German pilot later claimed to have shot him down.

name: Air France Flight 447
summary: Stalled into the Atlantic in a storm. The black boxes were recovered two years later from 3,900 m.

name: BSAA Star Dust
summary: Vanished over the Andes after sending the cryptic Morse word "STENDEC". Emerged from the Tupungato glacier 50 years later.

name: BSAA Star Tiger
summary: Vanished near Bermuda. Its sister Star Ariel also vanished in 1949.

name: BSAA Star Ariel
summary: Vanished in clear weather between Bermuda and Jamaica.

name: L'Oiseau Blanc
summary: Nungesser and Coli tried to fly Paris–New York two weeks before Lindbergh and vanished. Possibly crashed in Newfoundland or Maine.

name: Flying Tiger Line Flight 739
summary: A military charter carrying 93 soldiers vanished over the western Pacific en route to Vietnam.

name: Pan Am Flight 7 "Clipper Romance of the Skies"
summary: Crashed between San Francisco and Honolulu. Bodies showed high carbon monoxide — sabotage was suspected.

name: Lady Be Good
summary: Overshot its base and flew 700 km into the Libyan desert. Found nearly intact 15 years later; the crew's bodies were found up to 125 km away.

name: Glacier Girl (Lost Squadron)
summary: Forced down on the Greenland ice cap with 7 other planes. Dug out from under 82 m of ice and flown again in 2002.

name: Northwest Airlines Flight 2501
summary: Crashed into Lake Michigan in a storm. The wreck has never been found despite years of sonar searches.

name: Malaysia Airlines Flight 17
summary: Shot down by a Buk missile over eastern Ukraine.

name: Tenerife airport disaster
summary: The deadliest accident in aviation history: two 747s collided on a foggy runway.

name: Japan Air Lines Flight 123
summary: The deadliest single-aircraft accident, on Mount Takamagahara. Its tail fin lies on the seabed of Sagami Bay, found 2015.

name: LZ 129 Hindenburg
summary: Burst into flames landing at Lakehurst, New Jersey, ending the airship age.

name: Airship Italia
summary: Crashed on the Arctic pack ice. The envelope with 6 men drifted off and was never found; Roald Amundsen died searching for survivors.

name: Roald Amundsen — Latham 47
summary: The great polar explorer vanished in the Barents Sea searching for Italia's survivors. A 2009 search found nothing.

name: Andrée's Arctic balloon "Örnen"
summary: An attempt to balloon to the North Pole. Their camp on Kvitøya — with undeveloped film — was found 33 years later.

name: Charles Kingsford Smith — "Lady Southern Cross"
summary: Aviation pioneer Charles Kingsford Smith vanished over the Andaman Sea. An undercarriage leg washed up on Aye Island, Myanmar.

name: 1950 British Columbia B-36 crash (Broken Arrow)
value: Mark 4 nuclear bomb (without plutonium core) jettisoned
summary: The first lost nuclear weapon. The bomb was dropped and detonated (conventional) over the sea; the wreck lies on Mount Kologet.

name: Tybee Island nuclear bomb
value: A 3.5 t thermonuclear bomb
summary: Jettisoned into Wassaw Sound, Georgia after a mid-air collision. Never found; probably buried under 5 m of silt.

name: Palomares B-52 crash
value: 4 B28 hydrogen bombs; one recovered from 869 m of sea
summary: A mid-air refuelling collision over Spain dropped four H-bombs; two spread plutonium on land. A fisherman's tip found the fourth in the sea.

name: Thule B-52 crash
value: Parts of a B28 H-bomb secondary possibly never recovered
summary: Crashed on sea ice near Thule, Greenland with four H-bombs. A BBC investigation claimed one secondary stage was lost under the ice.

name: 1956 B-47 disappearance (two nuclear cores)
value: Two nuclear weapon capsules
summary: Vanished over the Mediterranean carrying two nuclear capsules. No trace was ever found.

name: 1965 Philippine Sea A-4 incident
type: Douglas A-4E Skyhawk with B43 bomb
value: 1-megaton B43 hydrogen bomb
summary: Rolled off the deck of USS Ticonderoga with a hydrogen bomb aboard. Lies at 4,900 m, 130 km from Kikai Island, Japan.

name: Goldsboro B-52 crash
value: Secondary of a Mark 39 H-bomb still buried in a field
summary: Two H-bombs fell on North Carolina; one came within one switch of detonating. Part of the other is still buried 55 m deep.

name: Roswell incident
summary: Debris from a classified balloon became the world's most famous UFO crash legend.

name: Kecksburg UFO incident
summary: Witnesses describe an acorn-shaped object crashing in the Pennsylvania woods and being removed by the military.

name: Liberty Bell 7
summary: Gus Grissom's capsule sank after splashdown when its hatch blew. Raised from 4.9 km in 1999.

name: Apollo 11 F-1 engines
summary: Saturn V first-stage engines recovered from the Atlantic in 2013.

name: Space Shuttle Challenger
summary: Broke up 73 s after launch. A large fragment was found by a History Channel dive team in 2022.

name: Space Shuttle Columbia
summary: Disintegrated on re-entry over Texas. 84,000 pieces were recovered — about 38% of the orbiter.

name: Mir space station (re-entry)
summary: De-orbited into the South Pacific near Point Nemo, the "spacecraft cemetery".

name: Spacecraft Cemetery (Point Nemo)
summary: The oceanic pole of inaccessibility, where Mir, Progress freighters and soon the ISS are dumped.

name: Genesis sample-return capsule
value: Solar-wind samples
summary: Parachutes failed and the capsule slammed into the Utah desert; scientists still salvaged much of its solar wind samples.

name: Amber Room
value: 6 t of amber, gold leaf & mirrors — est. $500M
locNote: Last seen in Königsberg Castle (now Kaliningrad). Theories: destroyed in the 1945 fire, shipped out on the Wilhelm Gustloff or Karlsruhe, hidden in mines in Saxony or Thuringia.
summary: The "Eighth Wonder of the World" was looted by the Nazis from Catherine Palace in 1941 and vanished at the end of the war. A replica was completed in 2003.

name: Lake Toplitz Nazi treasure
value: Counterfeit pound notes (Operation Bernhard) recovered; rumoured gold & Reich archives
summary: In May 1945 the SS sank crates into this deep, log-choked Austrian alpine lake. Divers recovered millions in forged British banknotes; legends of gold persist. Diving is now banned.

name: Nazi gold train of Wałbrzych
value: Rumoured 300 t of gold, gems and weapons
summary: In 2015 two men claimed ground radar showed a buried train in a tunnel near km 65 of the Wrocław–Wałbrzych line. A 2016 dig found nothing, but the legend endures.

name: Project Riese tunnels
value: Suspected hiding place for loot; many tunnels still sealed
summary: A giant unfinished network of tunnels in the Owl Mountains (Poland) built by forced labour. Its purpose is unknown; prime ground for Nazi-gold hunters.

name: Rommel's gold
value: Gold, jewels taken from Tunisian Jews
summary: Legend says SS officer Walter Kirchner sank loot off Bastia, Corsica in 1943. Searches have found nothing.

name: Merkers mine Reichsbank hoard
value: 100 t of gold, art, currency
summary: Found in a salt mine by Patton's troops in April 1945 — Eisenhower, Bradley and Patton descended to see it.

name: Missing Reichsbank gold (Walchensee)
value: ~365 gold bars & currency buried in Bavaria, 1945
summary: The last Reichsbank reserves were buried around Mittenwald and Lake Walchensee in April 1945. Much was later taken by US officers; some is believed still hidden.

name: Stolpsee / Lake Stolp hoard
value: 18 crates of gold rumoured sunk 1945
summary: Witnesses reported crates being dumped into this Brandenburg lake near Himmlerstadt. Searches in the 1980s and 2000s found nothing. Very close to Berlin.

name: Hitler's gold in Lake Chiemsee
summary: One of many Bavarian lakes rumoured to hide Nazi treasure sunk in the final weeks of the war.

name: Yamashita's gold
value: Rumoured billions in gold looted across Asia
summary: Supposedly buried in tunnels across the Philippines by General Yamashita's forces. Treasure hunter Rogelio Roxas claimed to find a golden Buddha; Marcos seized it, leading to a $22B lawsuit.

name: Kruger Millions
value: Gold coins & bars from Pretoria (£1.5M in 1900)
summary: Gold that Paul Kruger's government moved east by train as the British advanced. Legends place it in the Lowveld or Mpumalanga mountains.

name: Confederate gold
value: ~$500,000 (1865) in gold and silver
summary: The Confederate treasury disappeared during Jefferson Davis's flight from Richmond. Part was stolen at Chennault Plantation, Georgia.

name: Oak Island Money Pit
value: Theories: pirate treasure, Templar treasure, Marie Antoinette's jewels, Shakespeare manuscripts
summary: Excavations since 1795 have found layers of logs, flood tunnels and a few artefacts, but no treasure. Six people have died digging.

name: Treasure of Lima (Cocos Island)
value: Gold, jewels and a life-sized gold Virgin Mary (~$200M+)
summary: Entrusted to Captain William Thompson of the Mary Dear during the Peruvian revolt, who allegedly buried it on Cocos Island. 300+ expeditions have failed.

name: King John's crown jewels
value: Crown jewels of England (1216) — priceless
summary: King John's baggage train was swallowed by the tidal flats of The Wash. The area has since been reclaimed as farmland.

name: Lost Dutchman's Gold Mine
summary: German immigrant Jacob Waltz supposedly revealed the location of a rich mine in Arizona's Superstition Mountains on his deathbed. Several seekers have died in the search.

name: Beale treasure
value: 1.3 t gold, 2.3 t silver, jewels (~$60M)
summary: Three ciphertexts allegedly reveal a buried treasure in Bedford County, Virginia. Only one has been decoded (using the Declaration of Independence). Many consider it a hoax.

name: Forrest Fenn treasure
value: Bronze chest of gold nuggets and jewels, ~$1–2M
summary: Art dealer Forrest Fenn hid a chest in the Rocky Mountains with a 24-line poem as the map. Found in Wyoming in 2020 after 10 years and 5 deaths.

name: Victorio Peak treasure
value: Claimed 16,000 gold bars
summary: Milton "Doc" Noss claimed to find a cave full of gold bars and skeletons, then blew up the entrance. The peak lies on the White Sands Missile Range.

name: Treasure of the Llanganates (Atahualpa's ransom)
value: 750 t of gold hidden by Rumiñahui
summary: When Pizarro killed Atahualpa, general Rumiñahui hid the rest of the ransom in the Llanganates mountains of Ecuador. Valverde's Derrotero (route) is still followed by hunters.

name: Lake Guatavita (El Dorado)
value: Gold offerings — Muisca raft found nearby (1969)
summary: The real origin of the El Dorado legend: the Muisca king, covered in gold dust, threw offerings into the lake. Multiple drainage attempts found some gold; now protected.

name: El Dorado (city of gold)
summary: The myth evolved from a golden man into a golden city, drawing Raleigh and many conquistadors into the Guiana highlands and the Amazon.

name: Paititi
summary: A legendary Inca refuge of gold east of the Andes, in the rainforest of Peru, Bolivia or Brazil.

name: Lost City of Z (Fawcett)
summary: Explorer Percy Fawcett vanished in Mato Grosso in 1925 searching for "Z". Kuhikugu settlements found since suggest large pre-Columbian cities really existed.

name: Montezuma's treasure
summary: Aztec gold lost during the "Noche Triste" in 1520. Legends place a hidden cache anywhere from Mexico City to Kanab, Utah.

name: Aztec gold of La Noche Triste
value: One gold bar found under Mexico City in 1981
summary: Spaniards fleeing Tenochtitlan dropped and drowned with much of their looted gold in the canals of the lake, now beneath Mexico City.

name: Tomb of Genghis Khan
value: Likely grave goods of the Mongol Empire
summary: Legend says the funeral escort killed everyone they met and horses trampled the site. Burkhan Khaldun mountain is the most likely area.

name: Tomb of Alexander the Great
summary: Alexander's body was displayed in Alexandria for centuries, then vanished from the records around the 4th century AD.

name: Tomb of Cleopatra & Mark Antony
summary: Archaeologist Kathleen Martinez is searching Taposiris Magna, west of Alexandria. Others believe it lies submerged in Alexandria's harbour.

name: Mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang (unopened)
value: Said to contain rivers of mercury and palaces in miniature
summary: Guarded by the Terracotta Army; the central tomb has never been opened. Soil mercury levels support ancient accounts.

name: Ark of the Covenant
locNote: Other claimed locations: Aksum (Ethiopia), Mount Nebo (Jordan), beneath the Temple Mount.
summary: Disappeared when the Babylonians sacked Jerusalem. The Ethiopian Orthodox Church claims it rests in Aksum.

name: Ark of the Covenant — Aksum claim
summary: Kept in a chapel of the Church of Our Lady Mary of Zion, seen only by a single guardian monk.

name: Copper Scroll treasure
value: 64 caches, ~4,600 talents of gold & silver
summary: A Dead Sea Scroll engraved on copper that lists hidden treasure locations around Judea. None has been found.

name: Templar treasure
summary: When the Templars were arrested in 1307 their treasure supposedly left La Rochelle on 18 ships. Theories range from Rosslyn Chapel to Oak Island.

name: Rennes-le-Château treasure
summary: Abbé Saunière's sudden wealth sparked legends of Visigoth or Cathar treasure. Digging is now banned in the village.

name: Cathar treasure of Montségur
summary: Before the fortress fell in 1244, four Cathars escaped with the "treasure" — some say the Holy Grail.

name: Treasure of Alaric
value: Loot of the Sack of Rome (410), possibly including the Temple Menorah
summary: Alaric was buried with his treasure in the bed of the Busento river at Cosenza, which was temporarily diverted. Never found.

name: Nibelung treasure (Rheingold)
summary: In the Nibelungenlied, Hagen sinks the hoard into the Rhine near Worms. Hunters still scan the old river bed.

name: Priam's Treasure
value: Gold diadems, 8,000+ gold rings — now in Moscow
summary: Schliemann smuggled it out of Turkey; it vanished from Berlin in 1945 and resurfaced in Moscow's Pushkin Museum in 1993.

name: Staffordshire Hoard
value: 5 kg of gold, 4,600 items (£3.3M)
summary: The largest hoard of Anglo-Saxon gold ever found, unearthed by a metal detectorist in a farmer's field.

name: Sutton Hoo ship burial
value: Gold buckle, helmet, garnet jewellery
summary: A 27 m ghost ship buried with a king, probably Rædwald.

name: Hoxne Hoard
value: 15,234 Roman coins, gold jewellery
discoveredBy: Eric Lawes (looking for a lost hammer)
summary: Found by a farmer searching for a lost hammer. The hammer is now displayed with the hoard at the British Museum.

name: Eberswalde Hoard
value: 81 gold objects, 2.6 kg
summary: The largest prehistoric gold hoard in Germany — looted by the Soviets in 1945 and now in Moscow. Found an hour from Berlin.

name: Nebra sky disc
summary: The oldest concrete depiction of the cosmos. Recovered from black-market dealers in a police sting operation in Basel.

name: Cheapside Hoard
value: 500 pieces of Elizabethan/Jacobean jewellery
summary: Found by workmen demolishing a building in the City of London.

name: Panagyurishte Treasure
value: 6 kg of 23-carat gold vessels
summary: Found by three brothers digging clay for a tile factory in Bulgaria.

name: Varna Necropolis gold
value: The oldest processed gold in the world (4500 BC)
summary: A cemetery containing the oldest gold treasure ever found.

name: Bactrian Gold (Tillya Tepe)
value: 20,000 gold ornaments
summary: Hidden in a Kabul bank vault through the Taliban era by museum staff, revealed safe in 2003.

name: Padmanabhaswamy Temple vaults
value: $20B+ found; Vault B still sealed
summary: In 2011 court-ordered inspections found gold idols, thrones and coins in Kerala's temple vaults. Vault B, said to be cursed, remains unopened.

name: Kolchak's gold (Imperial Russian reserve)
value: Up to 200 t of the missing Imperial gold reserve
summary: Part of the gold train of Admiral Kolchak vanished during the Civil War; one legend says railway cars plunged through the ice of Lake Baikal.

name: Irish Crown Jewels
value: Jewelled star and badge of the Order of St Patrick
summary: Stolen from Dublin Castle in 1907 and never recovered.

name: Honjo Masamune
summary: The most famous Japanese sword, handed to a US soldier in 1946 and never seen again.

name: Library of Ivan the Terrible
summary: A collection of Byzantine manuscripts said to be hidden in tunnels beneath the Moscow Kremlin.

name: Captain Kidd's treasure (Gardiners Island)
value: Gold, silver, gems — recovered 1699 as evidence
summary: The only Kidd treasure ever confirmed — dug up and used as evidence at his trial. Legends of further caches stretch from Nova Scotia to the South China Sea.

name: Jean Lafitte's treasure
summary: The Gulf pirate is rumoured to have buried treasure around Galveston, the Louisiana bayous and Lake Borgne.

name: Mosby's treasure
value: Gold, silver & jewels taken from Union Gen. Stoughton
summary: Confederate raider John Mosby is said to have buried a sack of loot between two pine trees in Fauquier County, Virginia.

name: Padre Island lost treasure
summary: Shipwreck coins wash up on Padre Island; legends tell of buried pirate and Spanish caches in the dunes.

name: Benito Bonito's treasure
summary: Another of the three legendary hoards said to be on Cocos Island, the real "Treasure Island".

name: Pinaki church treasure (Tuamotus)
value: Gold from the Cathedral of Pisco
summary: Four sailors supposedly hid looted church gold in the lagoon of Pinaki atoll. Expeditions in the 1930s found nothing.

name: Loch Arkaig treasure
value: 40,000 Louis d'or sent by France for Bonnie Prince Charlie
summary: French gold landed too late for Culloden and was buried near Loch Arkaig. Most was embezzled; the rest was never found.

name: Friedrichshain Flak Tower lost art
value: 400+ paintings (Caravaggio, Rubens), sculptures
summary: Masterpieces of Berlin's museums stored in the flak tower in Volkspark Friedrichshain were lost in mysterious fires in May 1945. Some may have been looted rather than burned. In your city.

name: Atlantis
locNote: Plato placed it "beyond the Pillars of Heracles". Candidate sites shown separately: Santorini, Doñana (Spain), the Richat Structure, the Azores.
summary: Plato's island empire that sank "in a single day and night of misfortune". Almost certainly a philosophical allegory, yet hunted for 2,400 years.

name: Atlantis — Santorini (Thera) theory
summary: The Bronze Age Minoan eruption destroyed Akrotiri and may have inspired the Atlantis story.

name: Atlantis — Doñana marshes theory
summary: Some researchers link Atlantis to Tartessos, a lost Iron Age kingdom near Cádiz.

name: Atlantis — Richat Structure theory
summary: The concentric "Eye of the Sahara" matches Plato's ringed city in internet theories — geologists say it is an eroded dome.

name: Lemuria
summary: A 19th-century hypothesis to explain lemur fossils, later adopted by occultists. Plate tectonics made it obsolete.

name: Kumari Kandam
summary: A legendary lost Tamil land south of India swallowed by the sea.

name: Mu
summary: A Pacific continent invented by Augustus Le Plongeon and James Churchward.

name: Hy-Brasil
summary: A phantom island west of Ireland, visible only one day every seven years. Appeared on maps until the 1860s.

name: Ys
summary: King Gradlon's city in the Bay of Douarnenez, drowned when his daughter Dahut opened the sea gates.

name: Lyonesse
summary: Tristan's homeland, said to lie drowned between Land's End and the Isles of Scilly.

name: Cantre'r Gwaelod
summary: The "Welsh Atlantis" under Cardigan Bay. Submerged prehistoric forests appear at low tide at Borth.

name: Vineta
summary: A rich Baltic trading city swallowed by the sea for its arrogance, perhaps based on the real Slavic port of Jumne/Wolin. Its bells are said to ring on Easter.

name: Rungholt
summary: A North Frisian trading town destroyed by the Grote Mandrenke storm surge. Long thought legend; its church remains were located in the Wadden Sea in 2023.

name: Kitezh
summary: A city that sank into Lake Svetloyar to hide from the Mongols. Pilgrims crawl around the lake to hear its bells.

name: Dwarka (submerged)
summary: Krishna's city in the Mahabharata, swallowed by the sea. Marine surveys found stone structures offshore; their age is debated.

name: Yonaguni Monument
summary: Massive stepped terraces under the sea. Some claim a 10,000-year-old ruin; most geologists say natural sandstone.

name: Bimini Road
summary: A line of limestone blocks claimed as an Atlantean road, as "prophesied" by Edgar Cayce. Geologists: natural beachrock.

name: Thonis-Heracleion
value: Colossal statues, gold coins, the Naukratis stela
summary: Egypt's great port before Alexandria, lost beneath Abu Qir Bay. Rediscovered in 2000.

name: Canopus
summary: Sunken temple city beside Heracleion in Abu Qir Bay.

name: Pavlopetri
summary: The oldest submerged city with a full town plan (c. 2800 BC).

name: Port Royal
value: Pewter, silver, a pocket watch stopped at 11:43
summary: "The wickedest city on earth", the pirate capital of the Caribbean, slid into the sea in the 1692 earthquake.

name: Baiae
summary: The Las Vegas of ancient Rome, drowned by volcanic subsidence. Mosaics and statues lie in an underwater park.

name: Doggerland
summary: The land bridge between Britain and Europe drowned around 6200 BC. Trawlers dredge up mammoth bones and stone tools.

name: The Flying Dutchman
summary: A ghost ship doomed to sail forever off the Cape of Good Hope. The future King George V recorded a sighting in 1881.

name: Caleuche
summary: A glowing ghost ship crewed by drowned sailors and warlocks around Chiloé Island, Chile.

name: Lady Lovibond
summary: Said to reappear on the Goodwin Sands every 50 years since a jealous mate wrecked her on her captain's wedding night.

name: SS Ourang Medan
summary: A distress call — "all officers including captain dead… I die" — then a ship found with its whole crew dead, faces frozen in terror. No registry of the ship exists.

name: Kaz II
summary: Found drifting off Queensland with laptop running and food on the table, crew gone.

name: Bermuda Triangle
summary: Blamed for dozens of disappearances; statistically no more dangerous than any busy ocean area.

name: Dragon's Triangle (Devil's Sea)
summary: The Pacific counterpart of the Bermuda Triangle, south of Tokyo near Miyake Island.

name: Sandy Island
summary: Appeared on maps (and Google Earth) for over a century until an Australian research ship sailed through it in 2012.

name: Frisland
summary: A phantom island on maps of the North Atlantic from the 1560s to the 1660s.

name: Saint Brendan's Island
summary: Discovered by Saint Brendan, it supposedly appears and vanishes near the Canary Islands. Expeditions were sent as late as 1721.

name: Thule (Ultima Thule)
summary: The northernmost land described by Pytheas around 320 BC — perhaps Iceland, Norway or Shetland.

name: Lost Colony of Roanoke
summary: 115 settlers vanished, leaving only the word "CROATOAN" carved on a post.

name: Inca gold of Lake Titicaca
summary: Legends say the Incas threw a giant gold chain into Lake Titicaca to keep it from the Spanish; Cousteau searched in 1968. A real submerged temple (Wanaku) was found in 2000.

name: Loch Ness Wellington bomber
discoveredBy: Searchers for the Loch Ness Monster
summary: Found by a team hunting Nessie with sonar, then raised in 1985.

name: Loch Ness Monster
summary: Not a treasure, but the most hunted "wreck" in Scotland — a 1934 photo hoax and millions of sonar pings.

name: Zhang Xianzhong's sunken silver
value: 30,000+ gold & silver artefacts recovered since 2017
summary: A rebel leader's treasure fleet sank in the Min River at Jiangkou. Long a legend; confirmed by excavations in 2017.

name: Lost Mine of Tayopa
summary: A fabulously rich mine said to have been sealed by the Jesuits when they were expelled from New Spain, somewhere in the Sierra Madre.

name: Lost San Saba Mine (Jim Bowie)
summary: Jim Bowie of the Alamo allegedly found a Spanish silver mine near the old San Saba mission in Texas.

name: Dutch Schultz's treasure
value: $7M in cash, gold & diamonds (1935)
summary: The mobster supposedly buried a safe in the Catskills near Phoenicia before he was shot in 1935.

name: D. B. Cooper ransom
value: $200,000 ransom — $5,800 found on a river bank in 1980
summary: A hijacker parachuted from a 727 over Washington state with the ransom and was never identified.

name: Palmyra Atoll
type: reef island, integral overseas territory, insular area of the United States
summary: uninhabited Pacific atoll and unorganized incorporated U.S. territory

name: Costa Concordia
summary: cruise ship that ran aground in a maritime accident in 2012.

name: Japanese cruiser Yūbari
summary: light cruiser of the Imperial Japanese Navy

name: SMS Viribus Unitis
operator: State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs

name: Akagi
summary: 1925 aircraft carrier initially laid down as a battlecruiser

name: SMS Greif
summary: ship launched in 1914; freighter converted to a merchant raider

name: MS Achille Lauro
summary: cruise ship launched in 1946; sunken in 1994

name: SS Admiral Nakhimov
summary: 1925 ocean liner converted to hospital ship

name: RMS Carpathia
summary: British ocean liner known for rescuing survivors of the RMS Titanic

name: ARA General Belgrano
summary: 1951-1982 Diecisiete de Octubre-class cruiser of the Argentine Navy

name: USS Maine
summary: second-class battleship of the United States Navy

name: HMS Rawalpindi
type: armed merchant cruiser, steamship, ocean liner
summary: 1925 ocean liner converted to armed merchant cruiser

name: MS Herald of Free Enterprise
summary: passenger and car ferry that capsized at Zeebrugge in March 1987

name: RMS Franconia
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

name: SS Irma
summary: Norwegian merchant ship sunk in controversial circumstances in 1944

name: Torrey Canyon
summary: Suezmax class oil tanker wrecked off the western coast of Cornwall

name: SS Lamoricière
summary: French passenger liner operated by the Compagnie Générale Transatlantique

name: SS Orsova
summary: ocean liner of the Orient Line

name: Wake Island
type: reef island, unincorporated territory of the United States, insular area of the United States
summary: coral atoll in the North Pacific Ocean administered by the US and also claimed by the Marshall Islands

name: MV Craigantlet
summary: container ship wrecked in southwestern Scotland 1982

name: Girona
summary: historical galeass of the Spanish armada

name: SS Dronning Maud
summary: Norwegian Hurtigruten ship sunk under controversial circumstances by German bombers during the 1940 Norwegian Campaign

name: SS Otway
summary: 1908 liner converted to armed merchant cruiser

name: Alexander Nevsky
summary: screw frigate of the Russian Imperial Navy

name: SM U-12
summary: German submarine in World War I

name: Trento
summary: 1927 Trento-class cruiser of the Italian Navy

name: RMS Caronia
summary: cruise ship built in 1948, scrapped in 1974

name: Antarctic
summary: Swedish steamship used for several polar expeditions

name: Nantucket Shoals
summary: an area of dangerously shallow water off the Massachusetts coast, USA

name: SS Arandora Star
summary: British ship sunk by U-boat in 1940

name: HMS Culloden
summary: 1776 Culloden-class third-rate ship of the line

name: HMS H11
summary: 1915 British Royal Navy H class submarine

name: Antonio López
summary: historic Spanish ship shipwrecked in Dorado, Puerto Rico

name: Q5092507
summary: cargo ship built in 1944, shipwrecked in 1973

name: SS Continental
summary: bulk carrier that sank in Lake Michigan off the coast of Two Rivers, Wisconsin, United States

type: three-masted barque, merchant vessel, sailing ship
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

summary: 1842 Cumberland-class third-rate ship of the line

name: HMS Port Napier
summary: 1940 minelayer destroyed in Loch Alsh, Scotland, by an explosion following an engine room fire

name: Hesper
summary: bulk-freighter steamship that sank in Lake Superior

name: Joys
summary: steamboat that sank in Lake Michigan

name: Lofthus
summary: Norwegian shipwreck near Boynton Beach, Florida

summary: wooden schooner barge that sank in Lake Superior′

summary: a candidate for the wreck of HMS Riant

summary: paddle steamer sunk off Kent in 1850

name: Rouse Simmons
summary: three-masted schooner sunk in Lake Michigan
